claims.claim: The output structure and conventions are the model's own best-judgment interpretation of 'plan-to-features format' with no skill invoked
claims.evidence: Agent's own report confirms it did not use the skill, per the baseline task instructions

eval_feedback.overall: Content coverage is essentially equivalent to the with_skill run — a capable model naturally converges on a similar requirements+features shape and doesn't miss scope details from a well-specified plan. The meaningful gap is structural/format fidelity: naming convention deviates from the skill's exact spec, and REQUIREMENTS.md section names/ordering ('Summary' instead of 'Overview', extra 'Cross-Cutting Acceptance Criteria' and 'High-Level Data Model' sections not in the template) diverge, plus no feature file includes a Dependencies section. This suggests the skill's main value for a detailed, well-specified plan is enforcing a consistent, predictable output contract (useful when handing feature files to multiple sub-agents or teammates) rather than improving content quality, which was already strong.
